result.summary: READ-ONLY review of src/security.ts redaction at exact target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895. Verdict FINDINGS (5: 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 2 LOW). F1 security.ts:18 URL scrub needs an http(s) scheme AND a colon in the userinfo, so https://<token>@host and ssh/postgres/redis URLs print verbatim via `config show` and `serve --check-config` (reproduced end-to-end). F2 :20 query scrub lists only token/key/api_key/password, so access_token, api-key, secret, X-Amz-Signature leak. F3 :13 base64 variant matches only at 3-byte-aligned offsets and not base64url, so Basic base64("svc:"+secret) survives. F4 :97 then :110 excerptText collapses whitespace after redacting, reconstructing a whitespace-bearing secret. F5 :7 + config.ts:28,47 short (1-3 char) credentials, legal per schema, break the generic query scrub and disable artifact guards. Review is read-only; no source changes. /workspace/repo untouched and clean at baseline 5672ead. Report + findings.json in /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/.
result.details:
Target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 verified in a disposable detached clone at /tmp/rv33/repo (git rev-parse HEAD). Assigned workspace /workspace/repo left at its bootstrap baseline 5672ead2a526e07fea9ed11e58b3725e42013527, clean (git status --porcelain empty), fetch-only.

Scope covered: src/security.ts (Redactor.text/value/contains, redactorFor, excerptText, publicWorker) and its consumers src/settings/inspect.ts, src/settings/load.ts, src/serve-command.ts, src/files.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/http.ts, src/cli.ts, src/config.ts.

F1 (HIGH, src/security.ts:18) reproduced twice through the shipped CLI: a config file with [git.ssh] push_url set to a passwordless-userinfo https URL, or an ssh:// URL with user:password, is printed unredacted by both `bun src/cli.ts config show` and `bun src/cli.ts serve --check-config`. The classic https://[REDACTED]@host form is redacted, proving the regex is the only guard for that shape. SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL is added to the secret set only by commandRedactor (src/serve-command.ts:47); the redactedSettings path used by config show does not include it (SECRET_KEYS, src/settings/inspect.ts:7-11). Suggested fix: scrub any userinfo for any scheme, and register the push URL as a credential.

F2 (MEDIUM, src/security.ts:20) exact-allowlist query scrub; 12 of 13 dummy shapes returned byte-identical output through both redactedText and commandRedactor.

F3 (MEDIUM, src/security.ts:13) base64 variant alignment sweep: prefix lengths 0,3 redacted; 1,2,4,5 leaked and base64-decoded back to the full secret. base64url of a secret whose std base64 contains +// is not matched. The only in-repo prefix, "opencode:" (9 bytes, src/providers/opencode.ts:66), is aligned, so the built-in path is safe by coincidence.

F4 (LOW, src/security.ts:97 then :110) whitespace collapse after redaction reconstructs a credential containing one space. Partially mitigated: excerpts are re-redacted at the MCP boundary (src/mcp.ts:40).

F5 (LOW, src/security.ts:7 + src/config.ts:28,47) a 1-char credential turns ?api_key= into a mangled parameter name so the value is kept, and makes files.ts:70 reject every dotted artifact path and files.ts:103 block every file containing that character.

Non-findings recorded in the report: secret-set completeness, correct redact-before-slice ordering everywhere, artifact overlap padding, and one latent asymmetry where renderEvent prints event.data unredacted to stdout while the persisted line is redacted (not currently reachable: all store.event payloads are {} or {run_id,status}).

All example credential-shaped strings in the report and findings.json are invented placeholders; no secret file was inspected and no real provider or infrastructure was contacted.
